0c04dd0f-498b-4bc9-9451-070da386823e.summary_md: A dominant King's Cup, going 20-7 with a +1651 cumulative spread on the back of a 12-0 start that included a 709-point demolition of Cedric Lewis in Round 12. The overall play was extremely tidy — a 1.75 average mistakes score, a 93.2% bingo find rate (only 5 missed bingos across 27 games), and just 5 phonies. All seven losses came in the back half against elite competition, four of them to Nigel Richards, and several were agonizingly close (−14, −12, and −54). The chief cracks were endgame equity leaks in Rounds 23 and 24 (54.7% and 57.0% win% lost), the only real blemishes on an otherwise clinical run.
0c04dd0f-498b-4bc9-9451-070da386823e.title: King's Cup 2019

331d202e-0e1b-4af2-9559-ec30cb9bc928.summary_md: A clean two-game sweep of Austin Shin, 2-0 with a +175 combined spread and a 510-point average. The play was exceptionally tight — a 1.20 average mistakes score, only 3.3% win probability lost per game, and a perfect 7-for-7 bingo find rate with no missed bingos or phonies across either game. Both games were fully annotated on both sides, and Austin's higher 2.05 average mistakes score (driven by a 3.3 in the opener) reflects the margin in what were otherwise high-scoring games.
331d202e-0e1b-4af2-9559-ec30cb9bc928.title: NSC 2019 Final

342e1637-8b17-458c-b367-b9b3ba753cbb.summary_md: Jesse went 3-4 against Nigel Richards across the seven-game final, out-bingoed his opponent 19 to 14 and found 95% of his available bingos, but was outscored 452.1 to 428.0 per game and finished 169 points down on aggregate spread. His play was clean throughout — a 2.36 average mistakes score with only one phony (DERMES, challenged off) and a single missed bingo — so the losses came down to Nigel Richards outdrawing and outscoring him rather than unforced errors. The Round 6 loss stands out as the one that got away, with 48% win probability leaked, while the Round 7 blowout and Round 1 defeat were largely a matter of Nigel piling up bingos.
342e1637-8b17-458c-b367-b9b3ba753cbb.title: 2019 WESPAC Final

38341b8a-a16b-4cd6-96f5-5b4c01864f95.summary_md: A strong 16-11 (+846) showing across 27 games, powered by an excellent 2.22 average Mistakes score and a healthy scoring margin (462.0 to 430.6). Bingo hunting was sharp — 61 bingos at an 89.7% find rate, with only 7 missed all event and just two phonies (both challenged off). The wins were often decisive, including a 586-point monster against Wayne Kelly and four blowouts of +150 or more, while most losses were competitive rather than errorful. The main leak was win-probability lost in a handful of high-variance games (Rounds 20, 23, and 30 stand out), but overall this was a clean, efficient tournament against a field the opponent stats confirm Jesse consistently out-played.
38341b8a-a16b-4cd6-96f5-5b4c01864f95.title: WESPAC 2023 (Las Vegas)

55b29df3-10fd-471b-9e87-135ed5bbb2f6.summary_md: Across 77 practice games against James Curley, Jesse went 58-19 (+5238 total spread), averaging 484.5 to 416.5 with a 2.18 mistakes score and 16.0% average win probability lost. He found 202 bingos (202/224 (90.2%) find rate) against 161 for the opponent, leaving 22 on the board (one every 3.5 games) and playing 21 phonies. His high game was 662. Both sides were fully annotated in 18 of the games, where the opponent averaged a 3.93 mistakes score and 36.9% win probability lost.
55b29df3-10fd-471b-9e87-135ed5bbb2f6.title: James Curley practice games

56fd9e2f-07d9-4a43-beb9-30e1d432843e.summary_md: A best-of-three final against Nigel Richards that slipped away 1-2, with a lopsided −304 aggregate spread. Jesse actually played clean, disciplined Scrabble throughout — a 1.73 average mistakes score, 75% bingo find rate, and zero phonies — but a 685-point Round 1 onslaught dug a hole too deep to climb out of. The lone bright spot was a commanding Round 2 (563-417 on four bingos), while Nigel's near-flawless play (0.40 mistakes, 1.6% win% lost across the two annotated games) ultimately decided the match.
56fd9e2f-07d9-4a43-beb9-30e1d432843e.title: King's Cup 2019 Finals

7c16ae2b-ec5a-4606-8612-3f2d92f77c64.summary_md: Jesse went 20-10 at WESPAC 2019 with a cumulative spread of +1331, averaging 467.2 points per game against 422.8 for his opponents. His mistakes score of 1.68 and 12.0% average win probability lost reflect consistently clean play, and his bingo find rate of 77/80 (96.2%) was excellent — 77 bingos with only 3 missed all event. He played just 2 phonies while opponents combined for 9.
7c16ae2b-ec5a-4606-8612-3f2d92f77c64.title: WESPAC 2019

b2aa32e7-ab1d-45c2-8d59-362eeec37cb1.summary_md: Jesse posted a strong 20-9 (+1689 cumulative spread) at NSC 2019, averaging 476.7 to opponents' 418.4 while finding 97.4% of his available bingos and holding a clean 1.66 mistakes score across the 18 fully-analyzed games. The tournament's backbone was an eight-game winning streak from Rds 19–26, capped by a 580-point demolition of Jason Keller. The nine losses were overwhelmingly close — four came by 22 points or fewer, including 2-, 12-, and 15-point heartbreakers — and opponents out-bingoing him featured in most of them. With only two missed bingos all event (GRANOLa, RINGLETY) and a handful of phonies, there was very little left on the board.
b2aa32e7-ab1d-45c2-8d59-362eeec37cb1.title: NSC 2019

cf677d39-81ad-4a59-aec9-227c38340572.summary_md: A tough 9–10 result against a strong field. Win% lost tells a sharper story than the record alone: the two cruelest losses (Round 18, −3 vs Chollapat and Round 19, −2 vs Odette Rio) had win% lost of 31.7% and 48.3% respectively — Jesse was steadily leaking equity in both, not just getting unlucky at the end. Round 19's 48.3% is the highest of either tournament analyzed and aligns with the 4.1 mistakes index (also the worst of the event). On the positive side, the dominant stretch through Rounds 6–11 showed consistently low win% lost (4–11%), capped by a monster Round 11 (605–445 vs Austin Shin at just 5.7%). The bingo find rate of 82.0% (41/50 opportunities, after removing one false-positive in R2) and a missed-bingo rate of one every 2.1 games suggest spotting sevens and eights was a meaningful area of leakage. Blanks drawn were below average at 0.79/game.
cf677d39-81ad-4a59-aec9-227c38340572.title: Jesse Day's (abbreviated) Causeway 2026

d1212bee-bc38-4f19-8619-6be460686182.summary_md: A dominant one-day performance with a 5–1 record and an average winning margin of +83 points. The cleanest games bookended the day — Rounds 1 and 6 had win% lost of just 1.5% and 2.4%, both against familiar opponents. The sole loss came in Round 5 against Chris Canik (who bingoed three times), and Jesse gave away 35.2% of win probability that game — the highest of the tournament, suggesting the deficit was built steadily rather than from a single blunder. Round 3 was the outlier on the winning side: a phony played and two missed bingos (COURANTO and DOGGEDLY) contributed to a 29% win% lost despite a comfortable result. The biggest cautionary stat is Round 4 — a win over Becky Dyer by 72 points that still left 62 endgame spread points behind, primarily from failing to play out a lone L tile while Becky held an unplayable Q.
d1212bee-bc38-4f19-8619-6be460686182.title: Austin One-Day Aug '23

ffe31e07-d5fb-4937-bc08-691958053a8e.summary_md: A tough 1-3 finals set against Nigel Richards, ending at −214 spread across four games. The lone win in Round 1 was a commanding +150, but the losses ran the gamut: a −229 blowout in Round 2 where Nigel fired three bingos, a heartbreaking −12 in Round 3, and a Round 4 loss where four opponent bingos (and a 575-point board) outpaced Jesse's own three. The clean-play numbers were solid (2.42 average mistakes, zero phonies), but the story is bingos — Nigel's 10 to Jesse's 7, plus four missed bingos of Jesse's own, including a pair in each of Rounds 1 and 4.
ffe31e07-d5fb-4937-bc08-691958053a8e.title: 2018 World Scrabble Championship Finals
